# ᝯㄝₓ Plugin Suite for Stash

Curate a large library with ease and efficiency using a collection of synergistic browser-only plugins.

1. **A safety net under most operations.** Undo History records what the plugins write and what you save in Stash's own pages, pictures included, and undoes it days later ([not everything can be](GTTx-Core/README.md#what-undo-history-cannot-undo)). It checks every field first, so it never overwrites a later edit.
2. **Correlate scene [<abbr title="Scene Variants: scenes that are the same content - a full version and its trailers or cuts.">variants</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#variant) while keeping [<abbr title="The link from an entity in your library to its entry on a stash-box: the box's address and the entry's id.">stash-ids</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#stash-id) on full-length ones only.** Scene Variants associates trailers, promos and other partial versions of a scene and links them to the full one. It takes the stash-id off the partials and keeps the association in a custom field, so only the [<abbr title="Scene Variants: a variant that is the whole work, not a cut out of it - told by the Full-duration tag.">full-duration</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#full-duration) scene carries the [<abbr title="A shared online database of scene, performer and studio metadata that Stash matches against and scrapes from; StashDB is the best-known one.">StashDB</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#stash-box) id, as on StashDB.org itself. The set stays together on a Variants tab, its metadata kept in sync, and a set that drifts apart is flagged.
3. **Tags that keep themselves right.** Propagate carries tags and performers along 14 of Stash's relationships, Merge Performer Tags gives scenes their performers' tags, and Normalize Parent Tags [<abbr title="Normalize Parent Tags removing a tag an entity already carries through a more specific one.">prunes</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#prune) what a more specific tag already implies, or rolls [<abbr title="Tags nest: a tag's parents and sub-tags, and everything above (ancestors) or below (descendants) it.">ancestors</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#parent) up. All three can run automatically on save, and they take turns instead of fighting.
4. **Bulk editing Stash doesn't offer natively yet.** Custom Fields Bulk Editor covers the whole library, with locks and descriptions. Find & Replace searches every text field of every type. Entity Name Maintainer carries a rename everywhere the old name is informally cross-referenced. Tag Bundle Clipboard speeds up copying a set of tags from one [<abbr title="One item in a Stash library - a scene, image, gallery, performer, studio, group, tag or scene marker.">entity</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#entity) to another.
5. **Files and privacy.**
   - **Scene Filename Manager** renames files from templates and can always restore the original name.
   - **De-Spicer** anonymizes completely or tones down a whole library in place, with fine control: any field, including those Stash's own Anonymise leaves out, by the method you choose for each.
6. **Many small, optional user-experience and productivity improvements:** counts on headings, card counts on Scene Variants, a right-click Paste in tag boxes, an attention-grabbing warning when a [<abbr title="Stash's Scene Tagger, which matches scenes against a stash-box.">Tagger</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#tagger) candidate's duration doesn't match.

**Synergy:** Stash identifies the scenes using a metadata provider → Scene Variants links the duplicates and keeps the stash-id on the full scene → Propagate and Merge spread the implied tags → Normalize cleans the hierarchy → Find & Replace and Entity Name Maintainer tidy the text → Scene Filename Manager names the files, using Scene Variants' [<abbr title="The title a variant set's partials are named after.">base-titles</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#base-title). Undo History covers most steps. Installed together, the plugins ask each other instead of duplicating rules: [<abbr title="A custom field locked in Custom Fields Bulk Editor: added to, never changed or removed.">locked</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#lock) fields, [<abbr title="A tag implied by a more specific one on the same entity.">redundant</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#redundancy) tags, archived filenames.

**Yours to adapt.** MIT-licensed, plain JavaScript with minimal build step: change any plugin to suit your library, or build a new one on Core's shared parts.

**Warning: Back up your database and media library before installing!**

**How it was built and tested:** The code was written with Anthropic's frontier models, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1. They worked from the author's own curation workflows and from the limits those workflows keep hitting in Stash, with productivity as the goal. It is checked in several ways:

- a large automated test suite, on a harness that emulates Stash 0.31 and validates every GraphQL request against its schema
- memory measurements against extreme library sizes (100,000 scenes and 1,000,000 images, see [MEMORY.md](MEMORY.md)), and performance gates
- a delta review of every change, frequent reviews of the whole project, and blind adversarial reviews
- automated and ad-hoc live testing against a real library and mock-ups
- daily use on a library of several thousand scenes, performers, tags, studios and galleries, hundreds of groups and [<abbr title="A group (formerly a movie) collects scenes in order; a group can hold other groups, its sub-groups.">sub-groups</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#group), and a dozen markers
- a few quick checks against Stash's latest development branch

That still leaves room for issues nobody has found yet, in the many setups, combinations and library contents no test has covered.


The plugins are written to be installed **together**, and every one requires **ᝯㄝₓ Core**. They share one namespace, one visual language and a
handful of cooperation protocols, so two of their buttons in the same row agree on order and
spacing, a bulk run takes a [<abbr title="The flag a plugin holds while it writes, so the others do not react to its writes.">lease</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#lease) its siblings stand down for while it writes, and one plugin asks another
for an answer rather than reimplementing it.

Requires **Stash 0.31.0 or newer**.

## What they do together

Every plugin works on its own with ᝯㄝₓ Core. Install two of them and each asks the other the
questions only it can answer, rather than copying its rules. Nothing below needs configuring: a
plugin finds its sibling at load, and says in its log when one it would have asked is absent.

| This plugin | Asks | For what | Without it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Every plugin that writes | **all the others** | a shared **bulk-edit lease** while it writes, so the [<abbr title="A plugin's reaction to every save, switched on per entity type: Normalize Parent Tags' Auto-Prune and Auto-Roll-Up, Propagate's two directions.">auto-modes</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#auto-mode) stand down instead of reacting to every entity of a library-wide run | the auto-modes [<abbr title="A plugin's automatic response to a save you just made in Stash - auto-propagation, auto-prune.">react</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#reaction) to another plugin's bulk run, each possibly undoing part of the other |
| **Entity Name Maintainer**, **Find & Replace**, **Scene Filename Manager**, **Scene Variants**, **De-Spicer** | **Custom Fields Bulk Editor** | which custom fields are **locked**: a locked field's name, value and presence are left alone, and no Undo removes one (Scene Variants still adds its own field to a scene that has none) | nothing is locked, and each says so in its log. With that plugin present but unable to answer, every custom field is treated as locked |
| **Entity Name Maintainer**, **De-Spicer** | **Custom Fields Bulk Editor** | the **field descriptions** it keeps, so a rename - or a run's rules - can carry into the prose you wrote about a field | descriptions are not listed and nothing else changes |
| **Scene Filename Manager**, **Scene Variants**, **Propagate**, **Orphan Cleanup** | **Custom Fields Bulk Editor** | a **description filed** for the custom field they create or name, shown wherever that plugin shows a field | the field carries no description |
| **Scene Filename Manager** | **Scene Variants** | the **base-title** and **partial [<abbr title="What follows the base-title in a partial's title, before its index: &quot; - Promo &quot;.">postfix</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#postfix)** of a variant set for the `basetitle` and `variantpostfix` tokens, and a scene's **stash-id** for `stashid` | `basetitle` is the scene's title, `variantpostfix` and `stashid` are empty, and the log says so |
| **De-Spicer** | **Scene Filename Manager**, **Scene Variants** | the names their settings give the **custom fields they keep**, so a run leaves them alone | a field still wearing the collection's mark is left alone; one renamed in their settings is rewritten like any other |
| **Find & Replace** | **De-Spicer** | whether each word or phrase its **Term counts** export lists is already one of the **Explicit Terms** or holds one, and what it becomes, by De-Spicer's own matching, plurals included | the two De-Spicer columns are empty, and the log says why |
| **De-Spicer** | **Scene Filename Manager** | its **archive of original filenames**, so a scene's file is renamed only where Restore Original Filenames can take it back | no file is renamed, and the log says why |
| **Scene Variants**, **Propagate**, **Tag Bundle Clipboard** | **Normalize Parent Tags** | whether a tag is **redundant** under the hierarchy, so none of them copies a parent a more specific tag already implies | every tag is copied, and the sibling would prune it again afterwards |
| **Scene Variants** | **Entity Name Maintainer** | to **carry a renamed title** into everything that mentioned the old one, for every title it writes | the rename stands on its own |
| **Propagate** ↔ **Merge Performer Tags** | **each other** | a registry of the **relationship paths** each performs, so an overlap is noted in the log | overlapping paths are not pointed out |
| Every plugin that writes | **ᝯㄝₓ Core** | its **Undo History**: each pass and each automatic write is recorded, so it can be undone after the dialog has closed, in this browser; [not everything can be undone](GTTx-Core/README.md#what-undo-history-cannot-undo) | only the dialog's own Undo, while it is open (Core is always installed; a browser with no IndexedDB has no history) |
| **Merge Performer Tags** ↔ **Normalize Parent Tags** | each other | the lease above, in both directions: [<abbr title="Merge Performer Tags merging a performer's tags onto their scenes whenever a scene or performer is saved.">auto-merge</abbr>](GLOSSARY.md#auto-merge) stands down while the other applies, and the library-wide merge takes a lease of its own | each reacts to the other's writes, merging back what was just pruned |

Each plugin's own README has the detail, under **Relationship to the other plugins in this repo**.

## Installing

There is **no build step**. A plugin folder is copied as-is:

1. Copy **`GTTx-Core/`** and the folder you want — say `GTTx-NormalizeParentTags/` — into your Stash
   config directory's `plugins/` folder (`~/.stash/plugins/` on a default install). Every plugin
   here requires `GTTxCore`; installing through a source index brings it in automatically, but a
   hand-copied folder does not. Every folder starts `GTTx-`, so they sit together in Stash's plugin
   lists with Core first. **Coming from folders without the prefix** (`GTTxCore/`, `NormalizeParentTags/`…),
   delete those first: the settings are kept - they belong to the plugin, not the folder - and two
   folders holding one plugin load only one of them.
2. In Stash, go to **Settings → Plugins** and press **Reload plugins**.
3. Reload the browser page. Stash pins its plugin scripts at app boot, so a reload of the *plugins*
   is not a reload of the *script your tab is running* — the plugins say so themselves with a red
   banner and a **Reload UI** button when the two disagree, see
   [the stale-script banner and the Reload UI button](GTTx-Core/README.md#the-stale-script-banner-and-the-reload-ui-button).

Repeat per plugin. Beyond `GTTxCore`, nothing here depends on anything else being installed, and
every cross-plugin feature degrades quietly when its sibling is absent or older. **A plugin that
cannot find `GTTxCore` stops at load and says so once in the browser console** — Stash orders
plugin scripts by their declared dependencies but does not object when one is missing or disabled.

## Conventions worth knowing before you press anything

- **No write happens without a plan in front of you.** Every deliberate write opens a dialog listing
  every change first, with **Proceed**, **Stop**, **Copy log** and **Undo**. The auto-modes are
  the exception and say so in their own settings.
- **Shift-click ticks a range.** In any of these dialogs, click one checkbox, then Shift-click
  another, and every box of the same kind between them follows.
- **A caption ending in `...` asks before it acts.** One without it either writes nothing or stages
  something into the form in front of you, where Stash's own Save is the next step.
- **Orange means a control of ours writes; Stash's blue means it only reads.** Stash's own action
  buttons are gray, so orange is also how you tell one of these plugins' controls from Stash's.
  Every task button of ours is orange, and a settings row's button is Stash's blue - orange where a
  setting in the row writes on its own or narrows what the writes touch. The ⓕ, 🖬 and ⸎
  marks, warnings and a switch that risks something wear the **Highlighted Text Color**, which
  you pick in ᝯㄝₓ Core's UI Customizations (a yellow by default), beside the other colors.
- **An id in brackets is Stash's own database id** — the number in the URL — never a stash-id.
- **Backing up your database before the first library-wide run is strongly recommended.** A
  dialog's Undo reaches only what it wrote while open, and Undo History keeps the rest in this
  browser only - neither is a backup, and not everything can be undone: see
  [what Undo History cannot undo](GTTx-Core/README.md#what-undo-history-cannot-undo).
- **How much memory a task takes** in your browser tab, against 100,000 scenes and 1,000,000
  images, is in [MEMORY.md](MEMORY.md), measured again for every release.

## Contributing

- **`node .tests/run.js`** runs all suites. Most need no install; the `placement` suite needs
  `jsdom` and skips itself without it, so `npm install --prefix .tests` enables it. `.tests/package.json` exists only for
  that and is part of no plugin.
- **A new plugin starts at `version: 0.0.1`.** The major digit says the thing has been run in a real
  Stash, not that the code is finished.
- **Bump the version in three places in one edit**: the `.yml`, the `manifest` (including its
  `date:`, read off the clock), and `PLUGIN_VERSION` in the `.js` -
  `python3 .tools/bump.py <Plugin> [<version>]` does all three.
- **`RELEASES.md` is generated, never written.** A release *is* a commit that moved a `version:`, so
  run `node .tools/gen-releases.js` in the commit *after* the one that shipped it — a release row
  cannot name the commit that adds it.
- **READMEs and source describe the plugin, not its history.** No "since 1.2.0" in either; that
  argument belongs in the plugin's own `NOTES.md`, which does not ship.
- **Read AGENTS.md (in the [maintainer package](https://github.com/gregttx/GTTxStashPluginsRelease/releases/tag/v2026.10.15.1)) before adding a button, a dialog or a shared block.** Nearly every
  rule in it exists because something here guessed about Stash's markup and was wrong.
- **Releasing to the public mirror goes through `node .tools/release-drop.js`**, which
  copies an allowlist - never a denylist - and scans every staged file before it writes
  anything. See `.tools/README.md` (in the [maintainer package](https://github.com/gregttx/GTTxStashPluginsRelease/releases/tag/v2026.10.15.1)).
- **Claude Code hooks enforce some of this after every turn**, in `.githooks/claude/` (in the
  maintainer package, with a README saying how to register them): a plugin's docs left behind by a
  change to its source, a script changed without its version moving, a release missing from
  `RELEASES.md`, a new plugin starting above `0.0.1`, a hand edit to a generated file. A git pre-commit hook in `.githooks/` (in the maintainer package) refuses a commit
  that stages a plugin's script without moving its version, before the commit exists, and warns
  when a change to a setting leaves the settings inventory out, and a pre-push hook refuses a
  push carrying a file over GitHub's 100 MB limit; wire both with
  `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`.

## Forking and redistributing

MIT lets you change and redistribute any of this; keep `LICENSE` and its copyright line, and add your own for your changes. A few things let a fork run beside the originals rather than against them:

- **Give a changed plugin its own id** - its `.yml` filename and `PLUGIN_ID`. Stash keys a plugin and its settings by that id: a fork under the same id replaces the original, takes over its settings, and of two folders holding one id only one loads.
- **Take the ᝯㄝₓ mark off a changed plugin's name**, so its bug reports reach you, not this repo.
- **Keep or leave the cooperation protocols.** The plugins find each other through `window.__GTTx__`; a fork that keeps Core's protocols can share it, and one that changes them should use a namespace of its own.
- **Publish your own source index**, so Stash updates your users from yours, not over your changes with these.
- **Forking Core** is the hard case. Every other plugin requires `GTTxCore` in its `.yml`, stops at load without it, and binds Core's shared parts - dialogs, settings rows, Undo History, the cooperation protocols - through `window.__GTTx__`. So:
  - a Core under its own id needs a fork of every plugin installed with it, each `requires` changed to the new id;
  - a Core that keeps its id replaces this one for every plugin beside it - keep its exports and protocols, or they break;
  - a change only one plugin needs is often simpler made in that plugin, keeping Core as it is.
